critique: The warm amber, peach, and yellow lights against pure black now read convincingly as luminous bokeh rather than the earlier dark shaded spheres. The density is broadly appropriate and several lights have a pleasing bright core with a soft halo. However, the field is still not temporally coherent: almost every light has changed location from t1 to t4, with entirely new clusters appearing and prior clusters disappearing. This reads as particle turnover/re-spawning, not stationary decorative lights flickering independently. The remaining light edges are also slightly too defined for a soft flickering-light thumbnail treatment.

suggestions.why: Increase particle lifetime so the same emitted lights remain present across t1 and t4 instead of being replaced at new grid positions.
Lower emission proportionally while lifetime is extended, preserving a sparse field without accumulating a much denser particle population.
Broaden the halo around each existing bright core so the lights read more as soft glowing bokeh and less as sharply bounded circular sprites.
